web_evidence.title: The Odessa File — ebook sample
web_evidence.note: A sustained retail ebook sample presents Chapter One through a nonparticipating narrator, repeatedly narrating Peter Miller as 'he' while also reporting his thoughts; first-person material is confined to the author's note and character speech.

person_note: The story proper is controlled by a nonparticipating third-person narrator: the authorized opening narrates Peter Miller externally while accessing his thoughts, an interior passage does the same for Klaus Winzer, and a whole-book review explicitly describes third-person cross-cutting to the antagonists. First-person language in the quotes belongs to dialogue, testimony, an embedded diary, or the author's paratext and therefore does not create an alternating base structure. Confidence is medium because the input quotes are mostly gnomic, prefatory, dialogic, or clipped, and the strongest authorized prose source covers only the opening rather than the entire book.
